transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. It's really nice to meet you. Thank you so much for seeing me today. 

Um, well, I guess the main reason I decided to come in is just... I've been having a little bit of trouble with getting pulled off track? It’s probably just a normal thing that everyone deals with, but it feels like it happens to me pretty easily. Like, I’ll be working on finishing a dashboard for a project, and just one little Slack ping, or even a song lyric playing in the background, or a random idea for another project pops into my head... and suddenly I’ve completely lost the thread of what I was supposed to be doing. 

I really do try my best to stay focused, I promise, it just sort of slips away from me sometimes. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that okay.
Can you tell me if you often feel restless, have trouble staying seated, or act on impulses without thinking?

Um, well, I definitely try my best not to be disruptive! I'd really hate to bother anyone. But, I guess... if I have to sit completely still for a really long time, like through a long Zoom call for school, or if I just need to quietly work in one place... I do start to get this sort of... uncomfortable pressure in my body? 

It's probably not a huge deal, but it just feels like I really need to get up and pace around a little bit, or at least do something with my hands. I usually just try to quietly fiddle with a pen off-camera so I'm still being polite and paying attention. As for acting without thinking, I really do try my hardest to think things through so I don't make mistakes. 

Is that... is that the kind of thing you mean? I really hope that doesn't make me sound too immature or anything.
How often do you find yourself being pulled off track by distractions, and does this happen even in situations where you really need to stay focused, like during important tasks or conversations?

Um, I guess it happens... maybe a few times a day? It's really not all the time, I promise. 

When it's something really important, like if a friend is talking to me about something serious or I'm listening to a lecture, I try *so* hard to give my full attention. I'd just be completely mortified if anyone thought I was ignoring them or being rude. 

But sometimes, even when I'm trying my absolute best... my mind just sort of... slips away for a second? Like, I'll realize I missed the last sentence someone said because I noticed someone walking by the window, or I suddenly remembered an assignment I need to turn in. 

I always feel really awful when it happens, so I usually just try to quietly piece together what they said from context so I don't have to ask them to repeat it and bother them. I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad listener? I really do care about what people are saying, I just... get a little sidetracked. Does that answer your question okay?
Can you tell me if you often feel the need to move around or do something when you're supposed to be staying still, like in meetings or classes?

Um, well... I guess I do move around a little bit? I really try my best not to be a distraction to anyone else, though! 

But, um... like in my design portfolio reviews or when I'm sitting in class, I guess I do tend to... do little things. Like, I'll be bouncing my leg, or twisting my rings around my fingers, or maybe clicking a pen. Sometimes I'll just be shifting around in my chair trying to get comfortable. 

Usually, I don't even realize I'm doing it at all! It's just sort of a nervous habit, I think? But then someone will glance over at me, and I'll realize I'm doing it, and I feel so embarrassed. I always stop right away when I notice. I really hope it doesn't bother the professors or the other students too much... Do you think that's normal for someone my age, or is it something I should be trying harder to stop?

Can you tell me if these experiences with getting distracted or feeling restless happen in different parts of your life, like at school, at work, and at home, or if they're mostly limited to just one place or situation?

Um, honestly... I'm not entirely sure? I really hope it's okay that I don't have a great answer for that. 

Since I'm just focusing on my degree right now and don't have a job, I can't really say how I'd be at work. And when I'm at home... well, I try really hard to just be helpful and not cause any trouble for my family or my roommates. I don't *think* I'm too restless there? I mean, maybe I get a little sidetracked if I'm doing chores around the apartment, but I always make sure to get them done eventually so I don't let anyone down! 

I guess I mostly just notice it when I'm at school or doing homework, since that's when I'm really trying my absolute hardest to be a good student and pay attention. Does... does that make sense? I'm sorry if that's not very helpful!

Do you also find yourself getting distracted or feeling restless in social situations, like when you're hanging out with friends or trying to focus during structured activities like club meetings or rehearsals?

Um, I don't really think so? At least, I hope I'm not like that with my friends! 

When I'm hanging out with people, I really try to be fully present. I mean, maybe sometimes if we're just watching a movie or something, I might check my phone or fidget a little, but I'd never want them to think I'm bored with them. I care about my friends so much, and I'd hate to be rude. 

And for club meetings... I'm in a design club, and I always try to be super respectful when other people are presenting. I mean, sure, maybe my mind wanders for a second if someone is talking for a really long time, but I always try to snap right back to it. I don't think I'm any more distracted than anyone else would be... right? I really hope I'm not being a bad friend or a bad club member.
Can you tell me if you often struggle with organizing your tasks or keeping your workspace organized, even when you're trying your best to stay on top of things?

Um, well... I try really, really hard to be organized! I actually bought this really nice planner at the start of the semester, and I spent a lot of time color-coding my classes. 

I mean, maybe sometimes my desk gets a tiny bit cluttered when I'm right in the middle of a big design project? Just because I have all my sketches and materials out. But I always clean it up as soon as I'm done! I'd hate for my roommates to think I'm messy or disrespectful of our shared space. 

And as for my assignments... I don't think I struggle too much? I mean, I might occasionally misplace a syllabus or forget to write down a small reading assignment, but I always figure it out and get it done on time. I really don't want my professors to think I'm careless. I'm doing okay with that stuff, don't you think? Most college students get a little messy sometimes, right?
Can you tell me if you often lose track of time or find it hard to finish tasks, even when you're trying your best and there aren't any obvious distractions around?

Um... well, I really do try to finish everything I start! I don't want you to think I just abandon things. 

I guess... sometimes, like if a professor or a peer gives me a list of revisions for a design project, I might struggle just a tiny bit? Like, I'll jump right in and do the first couple of changes right away because I want to show them I'm taking their feedback seriously! But then... I don't know, maybe I'll get an idea for a different part of the design, and I'll kind of drift into working on that instead? 

And then sometimes I might realize later that I left one small—but, you know, important—change unfinished from the original list. I always feel so bad when that happens! I really don't mean to ignore their instructions. It's just that I get so caught up in trying to make the whole project look good. That's a pretty normal creative thing, right? I'm sure lots of art and design students get a little carried away sometimes. I really am trying my best to follow through on everything!
Can you tell me if the difficulties you've described with getting distracted or feeling restless have been happening for at least six months, and whether they started before you were 12 years old?

Um, wow, six months... yeah, I guess it's been happening for a while. I mean, I don't want to sound like I've always been a problem student or anything! I've always wanted to be good and make my teachers happy. 

But, um, I guess if I really think back to when I was little... like before I was 12... maybe there were some things? I remember in elementary school, my teachers would sometimes leave little notes on my report cards. They'd say things like I was rushing through my worksheets or that I'd kind of lose track of the directions. And, um, sometimes during group work, I guess I got a little too excited and might have talked over my classmates? I always felt so terrible when they pointed it out because I really just wanted to participate and be helpful!

And, well, my parents actually used to sit right next to me while I did my homework back then. Because if they didn't, I'd sometimes... I don't know, wander off to go look at something else, or I'd start drawing a picture before I finished my math problems. But kids are just naturally energetic and easily distracted at that age, right? I mean, I'm sure my teachers and parents knew I wasn't doing it on purpose to be difficult. I really was trying to be a good kid! Does that make sense?
